children.value: > Fact From Story Helena World Chronicle, which owns and publishes two weekly newspapers in Arkansas, argues that Google is “starving the free press” by sharing publishers’ content on Google, losing them “billions of dollars.”
> > Fact From Story Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.
> > Commonsense Knowledge Siphoning resources from a company harms that company.

> Fact From Story The case, filed by Arkansas-based publisher Helena World Chronicle, argues that Google “siphons off” news publishers’ content, their readers and ad revenue through anticompetitive means.
> > Fact From Story The suit points to Google’s older question-and-answer technologies, like the “Knowledge Graph” launched in May 2012, as part of the problem.
> > > Fact From Story By 2020, the Knowledge Graph had grown to 500 billion facts about 5 billion entities.
> > > Fact From Story Google compiled this massive database by extracting information from Publishers’ websites.
> > > Commonsense Knowledge A large database requires significant resources to create and maintain.
> > Commonsense Knowledge Knowledge Graphs take information from other sources.
> Commonsense Knowledge A company that loses revenue is being harmed.
